findings.message: AC-1 says the job should end a standing allocation "as ending it by hand does". It calls the same setStanding, but it throws away what setStanding returns. The `removed` month rows and the ended/dropped `standing` rows never reach the audit. The job's audit `after` only holds `{ through, slots, ended }`, and no event is sent for the ended slot. When the same thing is done by hand through `allocate`, the audit gets `before: { rows: removed, standing }` and an allocationSet event is sent. So the job now deletes up to 11 month rows per slot and keeps no record of which months or percents they were, which means a wrong end can't be traced or undone. The leaver handler (`endStandingForLeaver`) has the same gap. Fix: collect setStanding's `removed` and `standing` for each ended slot, return them in the service's `before`, and send the same allocationSet event (months [] , percent 0, standing true) that a hand end sends.
findings.scenario: Kasun Dias has a standing 30% on CON from 2027-01, and he leaves. extendStanding runs with today 2027-02-05 and deletes the 2027-03 to 2027-12 rows. The audit row says only `{ ended: 1 }`, and no event records the deleted months or their percent.

findings.message: The range text in the card is built once, from the first `a.month` and `a.through`. That text goes into the title, the `look.confirm`, the `done` line, and the confirm button label (`Add {person} to KEY, Mar–May`). The card itself has an editable Through field, and nothing rebuilds the label when it changes. This repeats the hr add-person-card lesson, where the title was built once from the first email. Fix: build the range in the label from the form's own fields (a `{month}`/`{through}` placeholder like `{person}`), or rebuild the card or note on edit, as `note`/`checkCardEdits` does for add_person.
findings.scenario: Ask "add Dinesh Wickrama to TMT from 2027-03 to 2027-05" and change Through to 2027-08 on the card. The button and the done line still say "Mar–May" or "Mar–May" while confirm writes six months, 2027-03 to 2027-08.

findings.message: entityToday relies on entityZone, and entityZone quietly falls back to "UTC" when an entity has no `workflows.entity_zone` row and its country isn't in ENTITY_ZONES. `ENTITY_ZONES` only knows Sri Lanka, which is why the test has to plant `Australia/Sydney` by hand. With no zone set, AC-5's "today in the entity's own time zone" turns into UTC, and the join date that gets saved is a day early near midnight. Fix: when an entity has no zone, refuse or flag it in addPerson. Don't fall back to UTC. Also add a test case that uses the Australian entity without the planted zone.
findings.scenario: The Australian entity has no entity_zone row (the fixtures don't add one). add_person runs at 2026-11-15T20:00Z, when it's already 2026-11-16 in Sydney. The person is saved with joined_on 2026-11-15 instead of 2026-11-16.

findings.message: The rule that until further notice can't have an end month, and its message, are written twice: once in proposeAllocate and once in the allocate service's `.refine`. If one copy changes, the card and the service can disagree. Fix: export one predicate and message from services.ts (or from a shared const) and use it in both places.

entityToday was inserted between entityOf's doc comment ("Exactly one legal entity: …") and entityOf itself. entityOf has lost its JSDoc, and entityToday now sits under two stacked comments. Fix: move entityToday above the entityOf comment.

The header comment is wrong and doesn't match the test cases. At 23:00 UTC it is already the next day in both Sri Lanka and Sydney, not "the same day in neither", and no case runs at 23:00 anyway: the same-day case runs at 06:00Z. Fix the comment.

The range suffix (`, Mar–May`) in the title, the look and the confirm button label is built once, from the months the card was first drafted with. But Through is an editable field on the card. If the person changes Through, the button still names the old range while the write uses the new one. This is the same class as the hr card title that went stale after an edit. Fix: put Through into the confirm label as a template field, the way `{person}` already is, or rebuild the label from the edited fields.
findings.scenario: The card is drafted for 2027-03 to 2027-05. The person edits Through to 2027-08 on the card. The button still reads 'Add Dinesh Wickrama to TMT, Mar–May', but confirming writes Mar to Aug.

findings.message: `addPerson` now decides joining or active by the entity's own today. In the same file, `recordLeaver` (line 88: `input.leftOn <= today()`) and the `hr.person.status` job (jobs.ts:11) still use today in UTC. So two status rules in one module can disagree about the same date at the same moment. Fix: send every status decision through `entityToday` for the person's entity.
findings.scenario: It is 2026-11-15T20:00Z, which is already 2026-11-16 in Sydney. add_person for Australia with joinedOn 2026-11-16 sets the person active. At the same moment, record_leaver for an Australian with leftOn 2026-11-16 leaves them active, because '2026-11-16' <= '2026-11-15' is false.

findings.message: Every row in the table leaves joinedOn out. No row passes an explicit joinedOn that is today for the entity but tomorrow in UTC. That is the status half of AC-5: before this fix it gave 'joining'. Add that row, and also a row where the explicit date is the next day locally, which must give 'joining'.
findings.scenario: joinedOn 2026-11-16 passed explicitly at 2026-11-15T20:00Z for Australia. No test asserts that the result is 'active'.
